NCLT Hearing - Update
Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited (AIM: MPL) provides an update following the recent hearing before the National Company Law Tribunal (“NCLT”), Mumbai Bench, in relation to the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of Karanja Terminal & Logistics Private Limited (“KTLPL”).
During the hearing on 27 August 2026, counsel representing the lenders / Committee of Creditors continued their substantive submissions before the Tribunal in response to the case previously presented by MPL.
As previously announced, MPL’s counsel has concluded its principal submissions, including presenting the detailed chronology and evidence supporting the Company’s case that Prudent ARC Limited intervened while KTLPL’s sanctioned One Time Settlement (“OTS”) remained in force and that subsequent actions resulted in the frustration and ultimate termination of the OTS process.
The lenders / Committee of Creditors have not yet concluded their submissions and will continue their arguments at the next hearing, which has been listed for 4 September 2026.
Following the conclusion of those submissions, MPL will have the opportunity to present its rejoinder and respond to the arguments made by the opposing parties.
The Company remains confident in the case and evidence it has placed before the Tribunal and will continue to pursue all available legal remedies to protect the interests of the Company and its shareholders.
Pavan Bakhshi, Managing Director of Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited,
commented:
“This hearing was the next stage in the substantive arguments before the Tribunal. The other parties have begun putting their case in response to the detailed evidence and chronology we have already presented.
Our position has always been clear: we want to pay the debt. The other parties will continue their submissions on 4 September 2026, following which our counsel will have the opportunity to respond.
We remain absolutely focused on protecting Karanja and the interests of our shareholders. We welcome the opportunity for all sides of this matter, and the evidence surrounding what happened to our OTS, to be fully considered by the Tribunal.”
MPL will provide further updates to shareholders as appropriate.

Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited (AIM: MPL) provides an update following the hearing before the National Company Law Tribunal (“NCLT”), Mumbai Bench, on 14 August 2026 in relation to the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of Karanja Terminal & Logistics Private Limited (“KTLPL”).
At the hearing, counsel for MPL continued his submissions before the Tribunal, presenting in detail the chronology and evidence supporting the Company’s case that Prudent ARC Limited (“Prudent”) intervened while KTLPL’s One Time Settlement (“OTS”) remained in force and that the subsequent actions of Prudent and the lenders resulted in the deliberate frustration and ultimate destruction of the OTS process.
The Company’s submissions addressed the sequence of events that occurred while the OTS remained in force, including Prudent’s intervention after KTLPL had successfully completed the lender-led Swiss Challenge process and the subsequent actions which resulted in the OTS being terminated. The Company’s Counsel concluded his arguments and will have the chance to rebut the submissions made by the lenders’ counsels in the subsequent hearing.
Lenders / Committee of Creditors’ submissions will continue at the next hearing, which has been listed for 27 August 2026.
MPL will provide further updates to shareholders as appropriate.
Pavan Bakhshi, Managing Director of Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited, commented:
“Today we continued putting our case and the evidence before the Tribunal in detail. We have been fighting for nearly a year to protect our asset and our shareholders from what we believe was a predetermined outcome. We will keep fighting as we have faith in the legal system.”

NCLT Hearing - Update
Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited (AIM: MPL) provides an update following the hearing before the National Company Law Tribunal ("NCLT"), Mumbai Bench, on 7 August 2026 in relation to the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process of Karanja Terminal & Logistics Private Limited ("KTLPL").
At the hearing, counsel for MPL commenced its substantive submissions by setting out for the Tribunal the detailed chronology surrounding KTLPL's One Time Settlement ("OTS") process and the subsequent involvement of Prudent ARC Limited ("Prudent").
MPL's counsel submitted that this chronology demonstrates that Prudent was permitted to intervene while KTLPL's OTS remained in force, notwithstanding that KTLPL had successfully completed the lender-led Swiss Challenge process, had been declared the successful bidder and had made substantial payments pursuant to the OTS. The Company continues to maintain that this was a clear breach of the agreed process.
Counsel further submitted that the sequence of events, including the subsequent termination of the OTS and changes to the process which followed, supports MPL's longstanding contention that the process was deliberately frustrated and ultimately operated to favour another party.
It was not possible to conclude the hearing on 7 August and MPL's submissions will continue at the next hearing, which has been listed for 14 August 2026.
MPL will provide further updates to shareholders as appropriate.
Pavan Bakhshi, Managing Director of Mercantile Ports & Logistics Limited,
commented:
"We have been fighting for nearly a year to save our asset from what we believe was a predetermined outcome orchestrated by the banks and Prudent. The chronology now being put before the Tribunal shows why we have held that position from the beginning.
"This has been a challenging time for the Company and its shareholders, but we have not given up. We now have the opportunity to put the full chronology and supporting evidence before the Tribunal, and we will continue to fight vigorously to protect our asset and the interests of all MPL shareholders."

company_30s.what_they_do: MPL is a logistics and supply‑chain services provider that handles freight, warehousing, and transportation for a variety of industries, from consumer goods to industrial manufacturing.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The company sits in a sector that is essential for keeping goods moving in a highly fragmented market. Its network of warehouses and transport hubs gives it a moat against new entrants, while its focus on technology‑driven inventory management appeals to large retail and manufacturing clients.
company_30s.current_state: MPL is in a turnaround phase. After a period of heavy debt and regulatory scrutiny, it is negotiating asset sales and restructuring deals. The business is still generating revenue but is under pressure from legal costs and a tight liquidity window. The share price is trading near the lowest point of the last 52 weeks, reflecting investor fear of a prolonged struggle.

rns_narrative: The company has been busy filing full‑year results, updating on debt repayment plans, and addressing court‑ordered hearings. These filings paint a picture of a firm trying to shore up its balance sheet while awaiting a potential cash infusion.

A second theme is the legal battle with the National Company Law Tribunal and other creditors. The updates suggest that MPL is negotiating a debt‑reduction package that could free up capital if approved.

A third thread is the rumor of a strategic partnership with the Adani Group. Several posts hint at a $700m investment or asset swap, which would provide a lifeline and a credible catalyst for a turnaround.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Skeptical optimism – people are waiting for a big deal but remain cautious about the legal mess.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A few traders are cheering the Adani rumor, saying it could turn the company around and unlock hidden value.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: The majority of chatter focuses on mounting debt, court proceedings, and the risk that the company may never exit insolvency.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Initially, posts were purely negative. Over the past week, a handful of bullish comments have appeared, but the overall tone is still wary.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for MPL are flat – no recent spikes in search volume, indicating that the crowd is largely silent and the market is not yet primed for a surprise.

near_term_catalysts: An official announcement from the Adani Group confirming a $700m investment or an asset‑swap deal.
A court‑approved debt‑restructuring plan that clears a significant portion of MPL’s liabilities.
Positive earnings surprise in the next quarterly report, showing improved cash flow and a clearer path to profitability.
Regulatory clearance for a key asset sale that could provide immediate liquidity.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in trading volume, a break above the 52‑week low, and a clear statement from management about the Adani deal or debt resolution. A sudden uptick in institutional buying would also confirm the thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the final stages of capitulation – the price has hit a deep trough and volume has dried up. If a catalyst arrives, the mean‑reversion engine is likely to fire, but the window is narrow; patience is required until a clear signal materialises.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the Adani investment is confirmed, MPL could jump to roughly 50‑70% of its pre‑crash level. That would translate into a 200‑300% upside from the current trough, matching the historical return of the RED and PURPLE signal categories. The asymmetry is strong because the downside is capped at the current price, while the upside is driven by a single catalyst.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the legal proceedings drag on or the debt‑restructuring fails, MPL may end up in a liquidation scenario, wiping out shareholder value. Even a modest downside beyond the current price is possible if the company cannot secure liquidity.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Maximum loss: the current share price (≈0p). Potential gain: up to 300% if the price recovers to 50% of pre‑crash levels. Risk‑reward ratio is therefore highly favourable for a contrarian stance.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a clear volume spike and a close above the 52‑week low. Size the position so that a 20% drop from entry would trigger a stop‑loss. Use a trailing stop that follows the price by 15% to protect gains while allowing the mean‑reversion to play out.
playbook.if_watching: Hold a small position until you see either the Adani announcement or the court‑approved debt plan. If either event occurs, consider a larger entry. If neither materialises within 60 days, reassess.
playbook.if_passing: If the company files for bankruptcy or is delisted, exit immediately. No position should be held if the legal process indicates that the company cannot recover.

ai_insights.bottom_line: MPL’s deep crash offers a high‑reward, low‑risk contrarian play that hinges on the Adani investment or a successful debt restructuring to trigger a sharp rebound.
